title: Agam Kuan, Patna - The Mysterious Ancient Well of Emperor Ashoka
content:
Agam Kuan, Patna

Agam Kuan, located in Patna, Bihar, is one of the oldest and most mysterious archaeological sites in India. Believed to date back to the Mauryan period (3rd century BCE), this ancient well is associated with Emperor Ashoka and has deep historical and mythological significance. Its name “Agam Kuan” means “Unfathomable Well”, symbolizing its great depth and mystery.

History and Significance

Agam Kuan is believed to have been built by Emperor Ashoka before he embraced Buddhism. According to legends, it was used as a torture chamber for prisoners during his early reign when he was known as “Chand Ashoka.”
Later, the site gained religious importance in Buddhism and Hinduism, as it is believed to be connected to Ashoka’s transformation into a compassionate ruler. The well is also considered sacred by local devotees who visit to offer prayers and throw coins for good luck.

Architecture and Structure

The well is about 105 feet deep and 20 feet wide, lined with ancient brickwork. The upper part of the well features arched windows and a protective railing. The greenish water and the ancient surroundings give it a mysterious and spiritual charm, attracting both historians and curious travelers.

Best Time to Visit

The best time to visit Agam Kuan is between October and March, when the weather in Patna is pleasant and perfect for exploring historical sites.

Entry Fee and Timings

  • Entry Fee: Free
  • Timings: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM
  • Closed On: Open all days

How to Reach

  • By Air: Nearest airport - Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, 8 km away.
  • By Train: Patna Junction is about 4 km from the site.
  • By Road: Easily accessible by taxi, auto, or local bus from any part of Patna.

Why Visit Agam Kuan

Agam Kuan is a blend of history, legend, and mystery. Whether you’re interested in Emperor Ashoka’s life, ancient architecture, or spiritual folklore, this site offers a fascinating glimpse into India’s ancient past and Patna’s timeless heritage.
